doc.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Chord scales story and first teacher Bill Shiner
summary: End of the chord-scale story, scales to blow off, and his first sax teacher Bill Shiner's beautiful sound.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I said, “Who came up with chord scales?” And he says, “I did.” This was crazy. This was like 300, 500 teachers back when I was talking to him. Now there’s about 800 teachers with the Conservatory merging in the last year or two with Berklee, the Boston Conservatory. But out of all the teachers, “I did.” And my first book for Warner Brothers Music, it’s about a 250 page book on improvisation, The Complete Book of Creative Improvisation. I call, instead of chord scales I say “scales to blow off.” To improvise off. And I said look, to my beginning students or whoever, whatever level, I said, “You don’t have to know chord scales, it’s a thing, I use it because it’s a helpful tool. If you have talent and you can move beyond that” — when I listen to Coltrane and Bird, I’d notate their solos, whatever I could as I was developing my ear when I was 14, 15. And I’d hear oh, it’s a ninth or something you know. Because my original saxophone teacher that taught Stan Getz back in the Bronx, Bill Shiner, he wasn’t an improviser. Beautiful sound on the saxophone. You’d be jealous. Just fill up the room with beautiful, old fashioned, with a little vibrato sound. And that’s this legacy, I have some of that. I have this sound. I think it’s a beautiful sound. I’ve gotten a lot of compliments, and it’s the one thing I feel I can give any student. And I tell my wife, I feel fulfilled if they don’t go any further with jazz or anything, if you’re getting my sound. Because I used to joke with them I said, “I’m not going to buy your CD if you don’t have a nice sound.” Because to me you’re not showing that you’re a good musician. Play classical, jazz, fusion, whatever you want to play, but have a nice sound that appeals to the ear. But Bill Shiner had that. And so I give them a lesson about embouchure. I say it’s just diaphragm and the lower lip. I don’t even care about the upper lip. Although my teacher taught me to play a certain way. I say you have the lower lip, I said I did everything wrong on saxophone with a great teacher. I used to clamp on the reed. And I had this, what someone called a peashooter sound, in a bad way. It was very small. And this is funny, I used to think when I was 14 years old, I’d blame it on my mother. I says, “Are you really my mom?” Because I’m this skinny little, tiny little kid with no sound. So I’m blaming it on my mom.
